newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan money rates close down, seen falling.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan money rates close down, seen falling.

text.p: Taiwan's money rates finished sharply down on Wednesday on excess funds, despite the central bank's persistent efforts to mop up liquidity, dealers said.

The overnight interbank rate ended at 5.856 percent against Tuesday's 6.081 percent close -- still outside the central bank's 5.00-5.5 percent target zone -- with 30-day commercial paper falling to 6.10 percent against 6.25-6.30.
The overnight interbank rate is likely to fall within the central bank 5.00-5.50 target zone on Friday, dealers said.
The central bank has issued negotiable certificates of deposits for three consecutive sessions to tighten liquidity in the banking system, but dealers said liquidity remained loose.
It issued T$5 billion in NCDs on Wednesday.
The bond market remained in a consolidation. The benchmark 86/4 bond yields are expected to move between 6.1200 and 6.1350 on Friday.
The money and bond markets are close on Thursday for the Labour Day holiday. They will reopen on Friday.
